fact: Lands Minister Hamat Bah said on 4 September 2026 that the government is developing a Land Information System to hold digital records of landholdings across the country, with World Bank-supported consultants working on it and a draft due by end-September, and that land-record archives are being digitised.

The National Land Policy 2026-2035 states that land administration suffers from the absence of a centralised Land Information System and a lack of cadastral data, and calls for a digitalised National Land Administration System.

A National Assembly select committee, reviewing a National Audit Office performance audit, found the entire land administration process paper-based with a fully manual registration system and no centralised database at the Ministry of Lands and Regional Government.

Dr Samba Sowe said the alpha version of the National Land Information System is complete and in testing, and that a company has been contracted to set up a data conversion centre to scan historical land records for it.

The Standard reports a contracted company is developing the digital land registry, with completion expected in 2027 and digitisation of existing land records among the priorities of a USD 10 million programme.
Minister Hamat Bah said a tender for the National Land Information System attracted nine firms, with evaluation and contract signing expected in early 2026.
